[id="using-the-v1-files-endpoint-with-external-s3-compatible-storage_{context}"]
= Use the /v1/files endpoint with external S3-compatible storage

[role="_abstract"]
After you configure the `remote::s3` provider, you can manage files by using the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/files` endpoint. File content is stored in your S3 bucket, and file metadata is stored in the Llama Stack PostgreSQL metadata store.

.Prerequisites

* You have configured the `remote::s3` provider for the `/v1/files` endpoint. For more information, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_llama_stack/using-external-s3-compatible-storage-for-the-files-api_rag#configuring-external-s3-provider-for-files-endpoint_rag[Configuring the external S3-compatible provider for the /v1/files endpoint].
* The Llama Stack pod is running and the `remote::s3` provider has initialized successfully.
* You have the `curl` command-line tool installed in the environment from which you run the procedure.
* You have the service or route URL for the Llama Stack API endpoint, without the `/v1` suffix.
* You have the API token required to access the Llama Stack endpoint, if your deployment requires authentication.

.Procedure

. Open a terminal session in an environment that can reach the Llama Stack API. The Llama Stack service is reachable in the following ways:
+
--
In-cluster access::
Run the commands from a pod in the same project as the Llama Stack service, or from a workbench that has network access to the Llama Stack service. The Llama Stack Operator names the service `<distribution_name>-service`. Use that name with port 8321, for example:
+
[source,terminal]
----
LLAMA_STACK_URL="http://llamastack-service:8321"
----

External access::
Expose the Llama Stack service by creating a route, and then run the commands from your local workstation. Use the route URL, for example:
+
[source,terminal]
----
LLAMA_STACK_URL="https://llamastack-route.example.com"
----
--
+
For more information about the correct base URL format and how to find the URL for your deployment, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_llama_stack/overview-of-llama-stack#openai-compatibility-for-rag-apis-in-llama-stack_rag[OpenAI compatibility for RAG APIs in Llama Stack].

. Set the `LLAMA_STACK_URL` environment variable to the URL of your Llama Stack service or route, without the `/v1` suffix. The example commands in this procedure append `/v1` as part of the endpoint path.

. If your deployment requires authentication, set the `LLAMA_STACK_TOKEN` environment variable to your API token:
+
[source,terminal,subs="+quotes"]
----
$ export LLAMA_STACK_TOKEN="__<api_token>__"
----

. Upload a file. The `purpose` form field is required:
+
[source,terminal,subs="+quotes"]
----
$ curl -X POST \
  "${LLAMA_STACK_URL}/v1/files" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${LLAMA_STACK_TOKEN}" \
  -F purpose="assistants" \
  -F file="@__<path_to_file>__"
----
+
In the previous command, replace `<path_to_file>` with the local path to the file that you want to upload.
+
[IMPORTANT]
====
The `purpose` form field is required.
If you omit the `purpose` field from the upload request, the endpoint returns a `400 Bad Request` error.
====
+
The output is similar to the following example:
+
[source,json]
----
{
  "object": "file",
  "id": "file-53b3fd75ca2c421c9a292ac63ff924ce",
  "bytes": 16,
  "created_at": 1778608944,
  "expires_at": null,
  "filename": "test.txt",
  "purpose": "assistants"
}
----
+
Note the value of the `id` field. You use this identifier in later operations to identify the file. The `expires_at` field is `null` for files that do not expire, which is the default behavior for files uploaded with `purpose="assistants"`.
+
[NOTE]
====
The response from the `remote::s3` provider does not include the `status` and `status_details` fields that are present in the upstream Llama Stack Pydantic model.
The `expires_at` field is returned as `null` rather than being omitted.
These differences apply to all responses from the `/v1/files` endpoint when the `remote::s3` provider is in use, including the list and retrieve operations in the following steps.
====

. List files:
+
[source,terminal]
----
$ curl -X GET \
  "${LLAMA_STACK_URL}/v1/files" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${LLAMA_STACK_TOKEN}"
----
+
The output is similar to the following example:
+
[source,json]
----
{
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "file",
      "id": "file-53b3fd75ca2c421c9a292ac63ff924ce",
      "bytes": 16,
      "created_at": 1778608944,
      "expires_at": null,
      "filename": "test.txt",
      "purpose": "assistants"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": false,
  "first_id": "file-53b3fd75ca2c421c9a292ac63ff924ce",
  "last_id": "file-53b3fd75ca2c421c9a292ac63ff924ce",
  "object": "list"
}
----
+
When no files are present, the `data` array is empty and the `first_id` and `last_id` fields contain empty strings.

. Retrieve file metadata:
+
[source,terminal,subs="+quotes"]
----
$ curl -X GET \
  "${LLAMA_STACK_URL}/v1/files/__<file_id>__" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${LLAMA_STACK_TOKEN}"
----
+
In the previous command, replace `<file_id>` with the identifier of the file, which is returned by the upload or list operation.
+
The output is similar to the following example:
+
[source,json]
----
{
  "object": "file",
  "id": "file-53b3fd75ca2c421c9a292ac63ff924ce",
  "bytes": 16,
  "created_at": 1778608944,
  "expires_at": null,
  "filename": "test.txt",
  "purpose": "assistants"
}
----

. Retrieve file content:
+
[source,terminal,subs="+quotes"]
----
$ curl -X GET \
  "${LLAMA_STACK_URL}/v1/files/__<file_id>__/content" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${LLAMA_STACK_TOKEN}" \
  -o __<output_path>__
----
+
In the previous command, replace `<output_path>` with the local path where the downloaded file content is saved.
+
The endpoint returns the raw bytes of the file. The command does not produce console output when you use the `-o` option. Confirm that the file was downloaded successfully by checking that the output file exists and has the expected size:
+
[source,terminal,subs="+quotes"]
----
$ ls -l __<output_path>__
----
+
The reported file size matches the `bytes` value returned by the metadata operation.

. Delete a file:
+
[source,terminal,subs="+quotes"]
----
$ curl -X DELETE \
  "${LLAMA_STACK_URL}/v1/files/__<file_id>__" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${LLAMA_STACK_TOKEN}"
----
+
The output is similar to the following example:
+
[source,json]
----
{
  "id": "file-53b3fd75ca2c421c9a292ac63ff924ce",
  "object": "file",
  "deleted": true
}
----
+
The `deleted` field is set to `true`, confirming that Llama Stack has removed both the file metadata and the underlying S3 object.

.Verification

* Uploaded files appear in the response from the list operation, with an entry in the `data` array whose `id` field matches the `id` returned by the upload operation, and whose `filename`, `bytes`, and `purpose` fields match the values that you supplied at upload time.
* Delete operations return a response with `"deleted": true`, and a later list operation does not include the deleted file in the `data` array. The corresponding object is also removed from the underlying S3 bucket.
* The Llama Stack pod logs record each operation as an HTTP access entry. For example, a successful upload is displayed in the logs as `"POST /v1/files HTTP/1.1" 200`.
